title: Grover's Search
summary: Amplitude amplification and inversion about the mean.
mission: Find the marked items among 16 possibilities. The variable num_marked holds how many items the oracle marks (M, different in each test): compute the number of Grover iterations (oracle followed by the diffuser) instead of hard-coding it. At the end, the marked items must concentrate the highest possible probability.

prediction.question: With 4 of the 16 items marked, how many Grover iterations are ideal?
prediction.explanation: With M marked items, sin θ = √(M/N) = 1/2, so θ = 30°. Each iteration rotates the state by 2θ = 60°, and one iteration reaches (2·1+1)θ = 90°: exactly 100% probability. Doing 3 iterations, as in the single-item case, would overshoot. The ideal number is ⌊π/4·√(N/M)⌋.

hints: Write the diffuser as a function: Hadamard on all qubits, X on all, multi-controlled Z (qc.h(3), qc.mcx([0, 1, 2], 3), qc.h(3)), X on all and Hadamard on all.
The circuit starts with Hadamard on the 4 qubits; then come the iterations, each with oracle(qc) followed by diffuser(qc).
Compute iterations = floor(pi / 4 * sqrt(N / num_marked)) (import floor, pi and sqrt from math) and repeat oracle(qc) and diffuser(qc) that many times.
